reviewNote: Draft based on common paediatric urgent-care guidance. Must be reviewed and localised by a qualified clinician before any release.

questions.label: Trouble breathing, grunting, or pauses in breathing
Lips or skin look blue, grey, very pale or blotchy
Unusually floppy, unresponsive or hard to wake
Weak, very high-pitched or non-stop crying that is not like usual
Repeated vomiting, or green or bloody vomit
A recent fall or possible injury
Far fewer wet diapers than usual
You feel something is seriously wrong
Measured temperature (°C), if you have one

rules.message: Breathing trouble needs emergency help now.
A blue, grey or very pale colour needs emergency help now.
A floppy or hard-to-wake baby needs emergency help now.
A fit or seizure needs emergency help now.
A temperature of 38°C or more in a baby under 3 months needs a doctor today, without waiting.
A weak, very high-pitched or unusual non-stop cry should be checked by a doctor urgently.
Repeated, green or bloody vomit should be checked by a doctor urgently.
Blood in the stool should be checked by a doctor urgently.
A swollen or hard tummy should be checked by a doctor urgently.
After a fall or possible injury, get a doctor to check your baby.
If your baby may have swallowed something harmful, get medical help now.
Trust your sense that something is wrong. Get your baby checked now, whatever a recording shows.
Feeding much less than usual is worth a call to your doctor or health worker today.
Far fewer wet diapers can be a sign of dehydration. Call your doctor or health worker today.
A temperature of 38°C or more is worth a call to your doctor for advice.
